title: Physics of the flying fish: glide data and Thompson's flight envelope
headline: TEST 4 RUN with the physiology chain: at its own muscle the real fish cannot power-fly (pass); at the pre-registered non-bird upper bound (a bat's 9.1 percent flight muscle, launch uncapped, flapping allowed) the model lets it fly 26 s bouts on its burst store (FAIL, reported plainly); and with the chain capping the launch the fish cannot lift off at all, so the tuned launch thrust of runs 5-6 is unphysical. The hypothetical flier with the chain on climbs to 179 m in 66 s and stops when the burst store empties (blood O2 store 35 percent): a burst, not sustained flight; it needs an air-breathing surface. Earlier: no accessible source gives mass, fin area and airspeed for the same flying fish; the fish is inside Thompson's envelope (v_min 9.85 m/s vs quoted 10-20); scaling law inconclusive; R2-R8 proved by Lean; 9 unsigned nanopub drafts; birds excluded throughout.
